Definition: akin to G3601; a pang or throe, especially of childbirth:--pain, sorrow, travail.
BiblicalUsage: Odin is a birth pang, the pain of childbirth, and by figure any sharp sorrow. Jesus calls wars and famines and earthquakes the beginning of sorrows in Matthew 24:8 and Mark 13:8, and Paul says sudden destruction will come as travail upon a woman with child in 1 Thessalonians 5:3. Acts 2:24 turns the word toward resurrection: God loosed the pains of death, because it was not possible that Christ should be held by it.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe birth pangs are the Bible's picture of the end: pain that means something is coming, not just something ending. That is why I hold that the sorrows of this age are not the last word, the pains of death were loosed, and the birth is on its way.
